about: Building blocks: what each landscape (and each block) is made of, as a dependency graph (a DAG). A parent lists its blocks under needs, each link with its kind (how the child feeds the parent: layer, a material blended into the parent's surface by a mask; scatter, instanced copies; base, geometry or base shape, joined as merge, part or surface) and its params (docs/PROCEDURAL.md "Composition from typed links"; DECISIONS.md "Typed building-block links"); a block must reach the Asset Studio goal score before its parent's new author rounds can start (docs/ASSET_STUDIO_GUIDE.md "Building blocks"). Block ids: a procedural asset is its library key (<category>-<asset>, catalog/procedural/library.json); a catalogue material is material:<id> (catalog/materials/materials.json); a planned block (a merge or part with no procedural asset yet: not built, shown as not started) is planned:<id> from planned below. tools/procedural/gen_blocks.mjs checks it (every id exists, every link has its why, no cycles) and writes the tab's copy (tools/evani-commons-tab/blockdata.js), the engine's copy (crates/evani-procedural-lib/src/blocks_table.rs) and the guide's table; crates/evani-procedural-lib's tests check it too.
draft: Draft for Chris to review (2026-11-08): every tree below is a first guess, worked back from each landscape's reference picture where it has one, else from its framing in ref_classes.json, else from its name and its category's framing. Change it here.
rule: Chris, 2026-11-08: every chain must directly help its end result. A block is a child only if it is a real visual ingredient of its parent (bark -> tree, pebbles -> boulders -> mountain, clouds -> sky), never an unrelated kind (no grass in the sky). Chains keep to their own kind (rock builds up by size, bark -> trees is its own branch); chains merge only where the combination is itself a real ingredient (mud + grass -> riverbank -> rivers). Every link says in one line why it helps.
